recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No current core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-42959; any broader Coding.system OID/UUID registry cleanup should be handled as a separate work-group decision.
issue_request: FHIR-42959 was Applied/Persuasive with Modification for the R5 Identifier section. It asked to remove the implication that UUIDs may be registered in the HL7 OID registry and to consider NamingSystem and cross-institution UUID guidance; the approved resolution replaced the sentence with shared-registry guidance, limited the HL7 OID registry to OIDs, and pointed to terminology.hl7.org NamingSystems for identifiers of broad international or national interest.
initial_application: The issue was applied before this reconciliation. Commit fa8905bbbb2f069b45a84a1550fdf4249c9091b9 attempted the change but left malformed text; commit 1192e15c8181cd012c1b77cc3b836f7144e67b5b corrected source/datatypes.html to the approved wording with links.
additional_context: FHIR-I minutes from 2024-04-22 confirm the approved scope and explicitly say Identifier.system has nothing to do with NamingSystem.url, so no NamingSystem.url explanation was approved. source/fhir.ini lists Identifier as an active datatype and routes datatype pages through datatypes.html. Adjacent Identifier issues FHIR-45479 and FHIR-41478 clarify globally unique values and custom systems, and existing combined audit commits already cover FHIR-26438 and FHIR-45479. A bounded adjacent search found old Coding.system OID/UUID registry wording, but no final applied Jira issue tying that separate Coding text to FHIR-42959.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The combined branch already has source/datatypes.html:1364-1367 stating that OIDs and UUIDs exchanged across institutional boundaries SHOULD be available in a shared registry, that the HL7 OID registry may be used for OIDs, and that terminology.hl7.org may register NamingSystems for identifiers of broad international or national interest.
